newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Film group urges HK protection vs parallel imports.
newsitem.headline: Film group urges HK protection vs parallel imports.

text.p: A U.S. film industry lobby group urged Hong Kong legislators on Monday to keep protections in a copyright bill against certain movie imports that it said would undermine marketing strategies and consumer choice.

Jeffrey Hardee, a vice president of the Motion Picture Association, urged the Bills Committee to retain protections against so-called "parallel imports" which compete with movies that are distributed by exclusive licensees.

"If protections against parallel imports were removed from the Copyright Bill, it is possible that all foreign products would be supplied by parallel imports with no localization at all, which will not be in the interest of the majority of Hong Kong consumers," Hardee said in prepared remarks.
MPA copyright owners work together with their exclusive licensees and it is in their interest that exclusive licensees' rights are protected, he said.
Parallel imports, though not pirated goods, disrupt the release schedule and undermine the marketing strategy of the exclusive licensee who has already paid the copyright owner a fee, Hardee said.
Hong Kong video rental companies argue they should be able to parallel import movies that exclusive licensees choose not to import themselves.
